possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: open-weight instruction-tuned text model with no reported evaluation or factuality guardrails, fine-tuned on large generated instruction datasets, so it can produce factually inaccurate content.

possible_risks.description: AI, and large generative models in particular, might produce increased carbon emissions and increase water usage for their training and operation.
possible_risks.justification: dense decoder-only 7B model fine-tuned on 3M+ instruction samples; training large open-weight models consumes compute and energy, and the card reports no environmental impact assessment.

possible_risks.description: Determining who is responsible for an AI model is challenging without good documentation and governance processes. The use of synthetic data in model development adds further complexity, since the lack of standardized frameworks for recording synthetic data design choices and verification steps makes accountability harder to establish.
possible_risks.justification: open-weight Apache-2.0 checkpoint with sparse documentation (no training-data provenance, evaluation, or governance details) makes responsibility for downstream use hard to establish.

specifications.model_size: 13.5 GiB of safetensors weights (14,483,530,784 bytes) in BF16

training_context.adaptations: The model is an open-source supervised instruction-tuning model and was produced by further fine-tuning the Infinity-Instruct-3M-Mistral-7B checkpoint; it does not use RLHF.
training_context.training_data: This checkpoint is a supervised fine-tune of a Mistral-7B base, trained on the Infinity-Instruct-3M and Infinity-Instruct-0625 datasets.
